newsitem.title: GERMANY: Concerns over Italy in EMU unjustified - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Concerns over Italy in EMU unjustified - Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, on the eve of a summit meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, insisted on Thursday concerns about possible Italian membership of Europe's single currency were unjustified.
"I am concerned about the distrust that greets Italy in many quarters. It's unjustified," Prodi said in an interview to be published in Germany's Handelsblatt newspaper on Friday.

Prodi is scheduled to meet Kohl just days after a Financial Times report that EU monetary officials were working on a plan to defer Italy's entry into Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), partly to assuage German fears of a soft euro.
Italy and other countries have denied such a plan exists while Bonn has said there had been no political talks on the matter but bureaucrats could be discussing it.
Prodi, reiterating comments he made in several Italian newspapers on Thursday, said a country's ability to meet the Maastricht criteria for EMU was the most important thing.

"Together with Bonn, we are of the view that the data available early next year are what count," Prodi told Handelsblatt in the interview. "All countries, including Italy and Germany, have to pass their exams, as Kohl has said."
He said Italy would not only meet the Maastricht targets but also adhere to the "stability pact" drawn up to ensure EMU members stick to budgetary discipline once admitted.
"There are precise values and we will stick strictly to them, and to the stability pact," the Italian leader said.
